primary_outcome_name: Self-reported physical activity level (Godin-Shephard Leisure-Time Exercise Questionnaire, LTPA-Q)
primary_outcome_instrument_scale: Godin-Shephard Leisure-Time Physical Activity Questionnaire (LTPA-Q), 3-item recall of weekly strenuous/moderate/mild leisure-time activity; total physical activity score (no fixed upper bound reported); classification cutoffs used for eligibility: <14 = sedentary, 14-23 = moderately active, >=24 = active
primary_timepoint: T1 = immediately post-intervention (end of the 12-week Lymfit program / end of 12-week wait period for controls)
contrast_reported_primary: Lymfit intervention vs. wait-list control (ANCOVA-adjusted post-intervention group difference)
population_detail: Young adults (18-39 years) newly diagnosed with lymphoma or up to six months after completing chemotherapy, classified as sedentary (Godin-Shephard score <14) at baseline; recruited from two university-affiliated hospitals in Montreal, Canada; N=26 randomized 1:1 (13 intervention, 13 wait-list control), mean age 32.35 years (SD 5.82; abstract states 32.1 years), 84.6% female.

published_estimate.quote: Next, the result of the ANCOVA showed that there was a significant group effect on self-reported physical activity levels at post-intervention (LTPA-Q: p = 0.002, intervention: M = 40.36, SE = 3.67, vs. control: M = 22.06, SE = 3.67) after controlling for the participants' score at baseline. (Results §3.4, p. 13 of 18). Table 3: 'Self-reported activity level 12.92 ± 5.01 [baseline intervention] / 11.04 ± 7.91 [baseline control] ... 40.36 ± 13.23 (32.77, 47.95) [post-intervention adjusted intervention] / 22.06 ± 13.23 (14.47, 29.66) [post-intervention adjusted control] ... Effect Size (ηp2) 0.348 (0.061-0.563) ... p-Value 0.002*' (Table 3, p. 12 of 18). NOTE: value=18.30 is the simple arithmetic difference of the two adjusted means reported in Table 3 (40.36-22.06); the paper itself does not state a single 'mean difference' number or its own CI/SE for the difference, only the per-arm adjusted means, per-arm SE=3.67, the partial eta-squared effect size with its 95% CI, and the ANCOVA group-effect p-value.
published_estimate.note_on_value: Not directly reported as a single contrast estimate by the authors; derived from the two reported adjusted arm means in Table 3. CI/SE of the difference itself are not reported.

B_covariate_list: Only the baseline (T0/pre-intervention) score of the outcome itself was entered as the ANCOVA covariate. Age and BMI (as listed in our registry covars_published) were NOT used as covariates in the model; they appear only as descriptive baseline characteristics in Table 1. The randomization stratification factor (chemotherapy completion status) was also not entered as a covariate.
data_availability_statement: The original data presented in the study are openly available in the OSF data depository at doi: 10.17605/OSF.IO/N5ABK.

registry_check.issues: (1) This is a pilot/feasibility RCT: the paper's actual stated primary aim is feasibility (a priori benchmarks for recruitment, retention, questionnaire completion, fidelity, missing data, Fitbit adherence, control-group design - all met), with acceptability as a second aim. There is no single outcome formally labelled 'primary outcome' for efficacy. The Methods/Objectives section lists 'preliminary effects on four study outcomes' as one aim, in the order: psychological need satisfaction (PNSE), exercise motivation (BREQ-3), physical activity level (Godin/LTPA-Q, our POST_Godin), and health-related quality of life (PROPr) - i.e. Godin/LTPA-Q is listed THIRD of four in Methods, not first. The Abstract, however, first names 'self-reported physical activity levels' among the ANCOVA findings, which is why this extraction used the abstract rule and picked LTPA-Q/POST_Godin as 'primary_outcome_name'. Because no true single primary outcome is declared anywhere, outcome_var_matches_primary is coded 'unclear' rather than 'yes'. (2) Covariate mismatch: our registry line lists covars_published='Age,BMI', but the paper's ANCOVA models adjust ONLY for the outcome's own baseline (T0) value, not for Age or BMI (these appear only in the descriptive Table 1, with a note of no significant baseline group differences). This should be corrected/flagged in the registry. (3) Minor numeric inconsistency in the paper itself: abstract reports mean age 32.1 years vs. Results/Table 1 reporting 32.35/32.4 years (SD 5.82) - not related to our registry, noted for completeness.

analysis_method_quote: Preliminary effects. All data analyses were conducted on R Studio (v. 2023.09.1+494). Independent t-tests were used to compare the mean values of all self-reported study outcomes at baseline between the intervention and control groups. Analysis of covariance (ANCOVA) models were used to compare post-intervention group differences for the study outcomes between the two groups, where the post-intervention values of the study outcomes were the dependent variables, the baseline (pre-intervention) values served as covariates, and the grouping variable identified the two study groups. Assumption checks for all data on the self-reported outcomes were first checked using appropriate statistical tests and plots. The normality of the variables was tested using the Shapiro-Wilk test. Two outcome variables (BREQ-3, Integrated regulation) and (PROPr, physical function) violated the normality assumption (p = 0.014; p = 0.040 respectively). Logarithmic transformation was applied to these two variables and the assumption was met afterward (p = 0.228, p = 0.059, respectively). Univariate models were used to examine the homogeneity of regression assumption on each dependent variable. Full-factor ANCOVA models were then fitted to evaluate the group differences in the post-intervention scores adjusted for the baseline scores. For this pilot investigation, an effect size of at least 0.2 for each study outcome was considered acceptable [52]. (Methods §2.6, p. 7 of 18)
notes: Pilot feasibility RCT (n=26, 13/13); the true declared primary aim is FEASIBILITY (recruitment uptake, retention, questionnaire completion, intervention fidelity, missing data, Fitbit wear adherence, control-group design), all a priori benchmarks reportedly met (Results §3.2). Acceptability (10-item survey, intervention arm only, T1) is a secondary aim. 'Preliminary effects' on four self-reported outcomes (PNSE, BREQ-3 exercise motivation, LTPA-Q/Godin physical activity, PROPr quality of life) are explicitly framed as exploratory/preliminary, not confirmatory primary efficacy endpoints - consistent with a pilot design (no formal power calculation was performed; target n>=12/arm was based on pilot-RCT sample-size conventions, not a power calculation). Multiple outcome-naming orders exist: Methods/Objectives lists PNSE first among the four preliminary-effects outcomes; the Abstract's results sentence lists physical activity level first ('...increase in self-reported physical activity levels, psychological need satisfaction, and exercise motivation...'); this extraction followed the task's abstract-first-named rule for primary_outcome_name given no formally declared single primary efficacy outcome exists. Post-hoc power analysis was conducted (G*Power) but the authors caution these should be interpreted with caution given the pilot nature (Results §3.4). No correction for multiple comparisons is reported despite many outcomes/subscales and p-values being presented. Randomization was stratified by chemotherapy completion status (completed vs. undergoing), but this stratification factor was not entered as a covariate in the ANCOVA models. Data are shared openly on OSF (doi: 10.17605/OSF.IO/N5ABK), consistent with registry data_file being an xlsx deposit.
